title: AWL Sublist 3
description: Tercera sublista de la Academic Word List: 60 familias clave para argumentar, describir procesos y presentar datos.

cards.definition: Another possible choice; different from the usual one.
cards.example: Wind and solar power offer cleaner alternatives to fossil fuels.
cards.warning: 'Alternar' (turnarse) es 'alternate', otra familia; en el AWL 'alternative' es 'opción'.

cards.definition: A fact or condition that affects a situation.
cards.example: Under certain circumstances, students may request an extension.

cards.definition: A written or spoken opinion; to give an opinion about something.
cards.example: Several experts commented on the lack of reliable data.
cards.warning: Es 'comment on something', no 'comment something'.

cards.definition: To pay someone for loss or damage; to reduce the bad effect of something.
cards.example: Higher salaries may not fully compensate for long working hours.
cards.warning: 'Compensa' (merece la pena) se dice 'it's worth it', no 'it compensates'.

cards.definition: One of the parts that together form something.
cards.example: Exercise is an essential component of a healthy lifestyle.

cards.definition: Permission or agreement; to agree to something.
cards.example: All participants gave written consent before taking part in the study.
cards.warning: 'Consentir' a un niño (mimar) es 'spoil', no 'consent'.

cards.definition: Large or important enough to have an effect.
cards.example: The project required a considerable amount of public funding.
cards.warning: No confundir con 'considerate' (atento, considerado con los demás).

cards.definition: Happening all the time or staying the same.
cards.example: The population remained constant throughout the 1990s.

cards.definition: To limit or control what someone or something can do.
cards.example: Many schools are constrained by tight budgets.
cards.warning: 'Constreñir' existe, pero en el día a día se traduce mejor por 'limitar'. 'Constraint' es muy útil en Writing.

cards.definition: To help to cause something; to give money or effort to something.
cards.example: Several factors contributed to the decline in bird populations.
cards.warning: Siempre 'contribute to + noun/-ing': 'contribute to reducing', no 'contribute to reduce'.

cards.definition: To arrange a formal meeting or to come together for one.
cards.example: World leaders convened in Paris to discuss climate targets.
cards.warning: 'Convenir' (ser conveniente) es 'suit' o 'be convenient'; 'convene' = convocar. 'Conventional' = convencional.

cards.definition: To organise people or activities so they work together well.
cards.example: A national agency coordinates the response to natural disasters.

cards.definition: The central or most important part of something.
cards.example: Reading and mathematics remain at the core of primary education.

cards.definition: Relating to a large company.
cards.example: Corporate tax rates vary widely across the European Union.

cards.definition: To match or be similar to something; to exchange letters.
cards.example: The rise in obesity corresponds closely with changes in diet.
cards.warning: 'Te corresponde a ti' (es tu turno/deber) es 'It's up to you', no 'It corresponds to you'.

cards.definition: Standards used for judging or deciding something.
cards.example: Applicants must meet strict criteria to qualify for the scholarship.
cards.warning: 'Criteria' es plural; el singular es 'criterion'. 'Tener criterio' (buen juicio) es 'have good judgement'.

cards.definition: To reach a conclusion by reasoning from the facts available.
cards.example: From the data, we can deduce that younger users are more likely to shop online.

cards.definition: To show clearly that something is true; to protest in public.
cards.example: The study demonstrates a clear link between diet and memory.

cards.definition: An official paper or file; to record the details of something.
cards.example: The effects of deforestation are well documented.

cards.definition: To control or have the most power or importance; to be the largest part.
cards.example: A few technology firms dominate the online advertising market.
cards.warning: 'Dominar' un idioma es 'master' o 'be fluent in', no 'dominate a language'.

cards.definition: Special importance or attention given to something.
cards.example: The new curriculum places greater emphasis on practical skills.
cards.warning: Se dice 'emphasise something' (sin 'on'), pero 'put emphasis on something'.

cards.definition: To make certain that something happens or is true.
cards.example: Governments must ensure that all children have access to education.
cards.warning: No confundir con 'insure' (asegurar con una póliza) ni 'assure' (asegurar a alguien de palabra).

cards.definition: To deliberately not include someone or something; to keep out.
cards.example: Low-income families are often excluded from the housing market.

cards.definition: A structure of ideas or rules used to plan or decide something.
cards.example: The report provides a framework for evaluating environmental policies.

cards.definition: Money for a purpose; to provide money for something.
cards.example: The research was funded by a government grant.
cards.warning: 'Funding' es incontable: 'more funding', no 'more fundings'.

cards.definition: To explain or make something clear by using examples or pictures.
cards.example: The graph illustrates changes in energy use between 1990 and 2020.
cards.note: Muy útil en IELTS Writing Task 1: 'The chart illustrates...'.

cards.definition: To come to live permanently in a foreign country.
cards.example: Many skilled workers immigrate to Canada each year.
cards.warning: 'Immigrate to' = llegar a un país; 'emigrate from' = salir del propio.

cards.definition: To suggest something without saying it directly.
cards.example: The results imply that smaller classes improve learning.
cards.warning: 'Implicar' en el sentido de 'conllevar' suele ser 'involve' o 'mean'; 'imply' es 'dar a entender'.

cards.definition: Happening at the beginning; first.
cards.example: Initial results suggest the new drug is effective.

cards.definition: A particular example or case of something.
cards.example: For instance, many cities now offer free bicycles to residents.
cards.warning: 'Instancia' (solicitud) es 'application'; 'en primera instancia' es 'in the first instance'.

cards.definition: To communicate or work together; to have an effect on each other.
cards.example: Children who interact with peers develop better social skills.

cards.definition: To show or give good reasons why something is right or necessary.
cards.example: The high cost of the project is difficult to justify.

cards.definition: A level or thickness of something lying over or under another.
cards.example: The ozone layer protects the Earth from harmful radiation.

cards.definition: A connection between two things; to connect.
cards.example: Scientists have established a link between air pollution and asthma.

cards.definition: To find the exact position of something; to put in a particular place.
cards.example: The new campus is located on the edge of the city.
cards.warning: 'Localizar' a alguien por teléfono es 'reach' o 'contact'; 'locate' es encontrar la posición.

cards.definition: To make something as large or effective as possible.
cards.example: Farmers use technology to maximise crop yields.

cards.definition: Small or not very important; a person under the legal adult age.
cards.example: The changes had only a minor effect on overall sales.
cards.warning: 'Menor' (más joven) es 'younger'; 'menor' (más pequeño) es 'smaller'. 'Minor' = poco importante.

cards.definition: To cancel the effect of something; to state that something is not true.
cards.example: Higher prices could negate the benefits of the wage increase.
cards.warning: 'Negar' (decir que no es verdad) se dice normalmente 'deny'; 'negarse a' es 'refuse to'.

cards.definition: The final result or effect of an action or process.
cards.example: Early diagnosis leads to better health outcomes.

cards.definition: A person or organisation that works or lives with another.
cards.example: The university works in partnership with local businesses.

cards.definition: The study of knowledge and existence; a set of beliefs guiding behaviour.
cards.example: The school's philosophy emphasises learning through play.

cards.definition: Relating to the body, or to things that can be seen and touched.
cards.example: Regular physical activity reduces the risk of heart disease.
cards.warning: 'Físico' (científico) es 'physicist'; 'Física' (asignatura) es 'physics'.

cards.definition: A part or share of a whole; the relationship between amounts.
cards.example: A large proportion of the budget is spent on healthcare.
cards.note: Esencial en IELTS Task 1: 'the proportion of people who...'.

cards.definition: To make information or a book available to the public.
cards.example: The findings were published in a respected scientific journal.

cards.definition: To act or behave in a particular way because of something.
cards.example: Markets reacted negatively to the announcement.
cards.warning: Es 'react to', no 'react at/before'.

cards.definition: To record a name officially; an official list; the formality of language.
cards.example: Students must register for their courses before the semester begins.
cards.warning: 'Registrar' una casa o bolsa (buscar) es 'search', no 'register'.

cards.definition: To depend on someone or something, or to trust them.
cards.example: Many rural communities rely on agriculture for their income.
cards.warning: Siempre 'rely on/upon', nunca 'rely in'.

cards.definition: To take something away from a place; to get rid of.
cards.example: The government plans to remove barriers to international trade.
cards.warning: Falso amigo: 'remover' (agitar) es 'stir'. 'Remove' = quitar.

cards.definition: An official plan or system (UK); a secret or dishonest plan.
cards.example: A recycling scheme was introduced in every neighbourhood.
cards.warning: En inglés británico 'scheme' es neutro (programa oficial); en EE. UU. suele sonar negativo ('trama').

cards.definition: A series of related events or things in a particular order.
cards.example: The diagram shows the sequence of steps in paper production.

cards.definition: The state of being male or female; biological category.
cards.example: The data were analysed by age and sex.
cards.note: 'Sex' suele referirse al sexo biológico; 'gender' al rol social.

cards.definition: A change in position, direction or opinion; a period of work.
cards.example: There has been a shift towards renewable energy in recent decades.

cards.definition: To state or describe something clearly and in detail.
cards.example: The contract specifies the number of hours staff must work.

cards.definition: Enough for a particular purpose.
cards.example: There is not sufficient evidence to support this claim.

cards.definition: A piece of work that has to be done.
cards.example: Robots can now perform many repetitive tasks in factories.

cards.definition: Relating to practical skills, machines or a specialised subject.
cards.example: Many young people lack the technical skills employers need.
cards.warning: 'Un técnico' (persona) es 'a technician', no 'a technical'.

cards.definition: A particular method of doing something that needs skill.
cards.example: New farming techniques have increased productivity.

cards.definition: Scientific knowledge used to create practical tools and machines.
cards.example: Technology has transformed the way students access information.

cards.definition: Based on good reasons or evidence; legally acceptable.
cards.example: Critics raise a valid point about the cost of the scheme.

cards.definition: The amount of space something fills; a quantity; one book in a series.
cards.example: The volume of air traffic has doubled since 2000.
